title.narrative: Contribution to the Special Fund of the Optional Protocol to the Convention Against Torture (OPCAT) 2020 -2021

description.narrative:
The Special Fund for OPCAT is a unique mechanism of torture prevention and the only operational fund established by an international human rights treaty. Its support to national preventive mechanisms, the establishment of which is a core obligation under the Optional Protocol to the Convention against Torture is key in preventing torture at the national level.
The main objective of the development cooperation is effective prevention of torture through supporting projects contributing to the establishment or strengthening of NPMs in developing countries, including Benin, Mauritania, Mali, Niger, Senegal and Togo, in accordance with OPCAT and recommendations of the SPT or through the support of their education programmes.

title.narrative: Laws on NPMs were drafted, discussed and advocated among relevant stakeholders, adopted and promulgated in accordance with OPCAT, as well as improvement in the operational efficiency of NPMs through adoption of strategic plans, guidelines and other tools.
No. of laws/legislative changes initiated and adopted, in compliance with the OPCAT; number or strategic plans, guidelines etc. adopted.

target.value: At least 2 draft laws on NPM’s establishment drafted or adopted; at least 3 visit methodology and strategic plans improved, operational tools and guidelines of NPM developed/revised/adopted in at least 6 countries.

actual.value: Legislative reforms and advocacy were supported by projects in Brazil and Togo; Improved standard operating procedures or institutional set-up of NPMs (e.g. Brazil, Kyrgyzstan) and visiting methodology (e.g. Hungary, Mexico) in 4 countries; Guidelines and operations tools were designed, developed and applied in 6 countries.

title.narrative: Knowledge and skills of NPM members and other stakeholders in torture prevention have increased
No.of trainings on international standards, reporting and monitoring techniques; number of study visits to other NPMs.

target.value: At least 12 trainings and workshops executed, at least one study visit conducted; pilot camp-court conducted in one country; monitoring visits to places of detention conducted in at least four countries, OHCHR NPM Practical Guide is translated into French, SPT advices are developed in user friendly format and provided to NPMs in Africa.

actual.value: More than 12 trainings and workshops executed; One study visit was conducted for Armenian NPM to Albanian NPM enhancing the capacity of the Armenian NPM, in particular lessons learnt from challenges related to COVID-19 outbreak, including monitoring of anti-COVID measures in institutions of deprivation of liberty by Albanian NPM; a camp court piloted in Togo to reduce the significant number of cases of pre-trial detention and overcrowding in places of deprivation of liberty; monitoring visits to places of detention were conducted in five countries (Brazil, Mauritania, Senegal, Togo and Ukraine); OHCHR NPM Practical Guide translated into French and distributed, especially among NPMs in Africa.

title.narrative: Collaboration between NPMs and other stakeholders has increased, as well as visibility of NPMs and awareness of torture prevention.

No. of meeting with stakeholders, number of collaboration frameworks developed, number of public meetings, campaigns and emissions, number of NPM annual reports produced and disseminated; number of leaflets, posters, brochures produced and disseminated, including in the places of detention.

target.value: At least 20 meetings with stakeholders conducted, information documents on NPM produced and disseminated in at least five countries, annual NPM reports produced and disseminated; at least one public awareness campaigns on NPMs and torture prevention conducted, NGO observatory for torture prevention established in one country.

actual.value: Most of the projects increased NPM’s collaboration with stakeholders (e.g. Brazil, Honduras, Hungary, Mauritania, Peru, Togo). Visibility of NPMs has been enhanced through different means, for example advocacy campaigns in Mali, community radio emissions in Senegal, social media in Brazil, development, translation and dissemination of annual report in Armenia. More than 20 meetings, roundtable discussions and conferences were organized through the projects for various stakeholders, including judges, advocates, representatives of NGOs, ministries, public defender’s offices, psychiatric institutions, law enforcement agencies, and prosecutors.

title.narrative: Establishment or strengthening of National Prevention Mechanisms (NPMs) compliant with the OPCAT leading to more effective prevention of torture.
NPMs are established or strengthened in accordance with the OPCAT and recommendations of SPT.

target.value: 25 projects supported in 15 developing countries, including at least 4 on establishment NPMs, at least 16 on strengthening NPMs, including drafting/revisions/adoption of NPMs laws; training of NPM members and staff; conducting self-assessment and drafting annual reports; elaborating visit methodology; improving collaboration among the stakeholders.
